items.title: Windows System Health Checker
items.summary: A PowerShell script that gives a first-pass diagnostic of a Windows PC in one run — instead of opening Task Manager, Settings and a command prompt one after another.
items.problem: When someone says “my computer is slow”, the first ten minutes are always the same: uptime, memory, disk space, CPU, network, last update. Checked one by one, by hand.
items.approach: Pull the data straight from Windows through CIM/WMI classes (Win32_OperatingSystem, Win32_LogicalDisk, Win32_Processor), convert kilobytes and bytes into readable GB, then finish with a summary that flags what actually needs attention — low RAM, no internet.
items.result: One command, one readable report. Along the way I hit an encoding bug that broke the parser with a confusing error — which taught me to be careful with characters in PowerShell scripts.

items.title: Windows Troubleshooting Toolkit
items.summary: A growing set of small utilities for the problems I see most at work — each one a chance to get better at PowerShell and Windows internals.
items.problem: The same handful of issues come up again and again: what's installed on this machine, what does the event log say, why won't the printer print, why is there no network.

items.title: IT Support Ticket Workflow
items.summary: A hands-on practice setup in Jira Service Management modelling a basic helpdesk flow — how a ticket moves from reported to resolved.
items.problem: I document and escalate incidents at work already. I wanted to understand how a proper ticketing tool structures that same process.
items.approach: Built a simple workflow with the statuses a support team actually uses: To Do → In Progress → Waiting for Customer → Resolved.
